description: Table 4 is a single, two-column data table rendered as an image, headed "Hardness [HV]". The table has one header row and one data row. The header row labels the two columns of the alloy's conditions: the left column is titled "Hot-Rolled" and the right column is titled "600 °C — Tempered". There are no additional rows, no error bars, no units other than Vickers hardness, and no graphical elements. The single data row records the measured hardness values: "401" under the Hot-Rolled condition and "420" under the 600 °C — Tempered condition. The table therefore compares only two states of one alloy. Per the caption, the alloy is 12Al-10Mn-1C (an Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steel), and the table is presented as an example of the hardening effect of a precipitation transformation. The citing text states that, for a medium-Mn steel with a high Al content of 12% tempered at 600 °C, the γ phase underwent a "generic precipitation transformation" not as ordered as discontinuous precipitation, and that this transformation "was been linked to slight hardening effects (Table 4)". The figure thus demonstrates quantitatively that tempering at 600 °C raises the Vickers hardness of the hot-rolled 12Al-10Mn-1C steel by a small amount, from 401 HV to 420 HV, i.e. an increase of 19 HV — a "slight" hardening effect consistent with the described transformation. No micrograph, curve or schematic accompanies the table within this group.

observations.observation: The table is headed 'Hardness [HV]', so the tabulated quantity is Vickers hardness in HV units.
The two column headers are exactly 'Hot-Rolled' and '600 °C — Tempered'.
The Hot-Rolled condition has a printed hardness value of 401 HV.
The 600 °C — Tempered condition has a printed hardness value of 420 HV.
Tempering at 600 °C raises hardness relative to the hot-rolled state (420 HV vs 401 HV), a difference of 19 HV.
The table contains only one header row and one data row; no other conditions or values are listed.
The caption states the table is an example of hardening effects of precipitation transformation on 12Al-10Mn-1C.
The caption states that depleted austenite is one of two variants of the phase, since globular carbides precipitated in it and not in the other grade.
The citing text states that in medium Mn with a high Al content of 12% tempered at 600 °C, γ passed through a complex random-like transformation linked to slight hardening effects (Table 4).
The citing text labels this transformation a 'generic precipitation transformation', described as not as ordered and defined as discontinuous precipitation.

subfigures.description: Single two-column table headed 'Hardness [HV]' comparing the Hot-Rolled condition (401 HV) with the 600 °C — Tempered condition (420 HV) for the 12Al-10Mn-1C steel.
